title: Hotfix: prevent Dedicated autoscaler scale-to-zero when predictor returns null
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description:
Context: During the Dedicated predictive autoscaling pilot we observed an unsafe downscale to 0 replicas when the forecast provider returned `null` for `predicted_replicas` (provider was up, but returned no value for the window due to insufficient history / timezone mismatch). In the current arbitration code path we treat `null` as `0` (via defaulting), then apply dampening/cooldown and clamp to bounds. For pilot deployments with `min_replicas` unset (legacy default 0) this allowed scale-to-zero, which is explicitly disallowed for Dedicated inference pools and caused queue build-up + increased p95 latency. This PR adds a guard: when predictive mode is enabled but the predictor returns `null`/missing, we treat it as "prediction unavailable" and fall back to the reactive desired (or keep last desired when reactive is also missing), never generating a new desired from a null prediction. We also emit an explicit reason code + metric so we can alert on predictor quality without impacting safety. Fix is scoped, low risk, and intended as an immediate pilot hotfix.

Changes:
- Autoscaler: treat `prediction == null` as unavailable and skip predictive arbitration for that tick.
- Autoscaler: ensure we never compute desired=0 solely from null prediction; decision reason becomes `predictive_unavailable_fallback_reactive`.
- Metrics: increment `dedicated_autoscaler_predictor_null_total{region,deployment_id}` and add decision log field `prediction_present=false`.
- Tests: add unit test covering null forecast with legacy bounds (min unset) asserting desired stays >= 1 for Dedicated (using existing "dedicated floor" safety invariant) and does not downscale compared to reactive.

Rollout:
- Ship as hotfix behind existing per-account pilot flag (no config changes).
- SRE to monitor bound-hit + queue depth + `predictor_null_total` for the pilot accounts for 48h.

Incident reference:
- Related to pilot oscillation / latency report and on-call thread; see SUP-28479 for customer impact details.

Checklist:
- [x] Added unit coverage
- [x] Verified no behavior change when predictor returns a valid value
- [x] Verified fallback is deterministic (audit fields set)
- [x] SRE sign-off for pilot hotfix
commits: dedicated/autoscaler: guard against null prediction and mark predictive unavailable
dedicated/autoscaler: add decision reason + metric for null prediction
tests: add regression test for null prediction scale-to-zero
docs/comments: clarify semantics in code for prediction unavailable fallback
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz (review): Can we confirm we are not changing behavior when the predictor is temporarily stale vs null? I want stale to still be treated as unavailable.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Yep — stale continues to be handled in the provider wrapper (returns unavailable). This PR only fixes the "present but null" case that was slipping through as 0.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add an explicit metric for nulls so we can see if this is happening often; also ensure decision logs include a boolean for prediction presence for auditability.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added `dedicated_autoscaler_predictor_null_total` and `prediction_present=false` in the decision payload. Updated the regression test to assert reason code.
Jordan Lee (review): For the test, can we assert we fall back to reactive desired rather than pinning to last desired? Otherwise we might hide a separate reactive pipeline failure.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Updated test to include a reactive desired and assert we follow it. If reactive is missing, we still preserve last desired (existing behavior) and set reason accordingly.
Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Approved. This is minimal and addresses the safety invariant. Please coordinate with SRE to roll to pilot accounts today.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved; hotfix is good to go. On-call will monitor `predictor_null_total` and queue depth panels during the next ramp.
release_notes: Dedicated: fixed an issue in predictive autoscaling where a null forecast could trigger an unsafe downscale; autoscaler now falls back to reactive scaling when predictions are unavailable.
